# hands/giveaway

Tiny Drops, public $TINY rounds paid by code.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/giveaway <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): open; judge
- Job (writes state or calls the core): entries [ID]; draw [ID]; settle [ID]; clawback [ID]; due
- Operator only (never call): none
- Read only: status [ID]; announcements

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `open` | A | `{format, pool_tiny, winners, best_reply_tiny, prompt, deadline \| deadline_hours, threshold?, text}` (`deadline_hours`, whole hours from now, for a drafting turn that is not told the time). |
| `status [ID]` | R | The season against the caps (`next_tag`, `season_left_tiny`, `rounds_left_this_week`, ...) and the last 20 rounds, or one round with its entry counts. |
| `announcements` | R | What the giveaway playbooks owe a post for: `open` (room to open a round), `countdown` (an open round within 24 hours of its deadline), `to_judge` (past the deadline, with a best-reply prize and no pick: the entries eligible so far, never a held one, at most 30, 500 characters e… |
| `judge` | A | `{round_id, entry_id, reasons, text}`, after the deadline and before the draw, for an entry eligible so far and not Teeny's. |
| `entries [ID]` | J | Every round not drawn yet: its entries from `hands.db` alone, never X (a test fails on any X call). |
| `draw [ID]` | J | After the deadline. |
| `settle [ID]` | J | A drawn round: the Merkle tree over (address, amount) hashed as the Rewards program checks a claim (keccak-256; `giveaway/merkle.py`, pinned to the program's Rust vectors), `clawback_at` `GIVEAWAY_CLAWBACK_DAYS` away, `authority` from `GIVEAWAY_AUTHORITY`. |
| `clawback [ID]` | J | A settled round past `clawback_at`: the chain step closes the distribution (CloseMerkleDistribution), which returns what nobody claimed to the giveaway wallet. |
| `due` | J | `entries`, then `draw`, `settle` and `clawback` for every round each is due for. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `announcements`, `clawback`, `draw`, `due`, `entries`, `judge`, `open`, `settle`, `status`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `DRY_RUN=1 hands/giveaway <verb> --help`. The full account is in docs/hands.md.
